meta.name: AGENTIC_BROWSER_PRODUCTION_MASTER_LOOP
meta.mission: Build and maintain a production-grade, long-term-supported AI agentic browser. Users state a task once; the agent performs it in the browser, learns the workflow, saves it as a versioned reusable skill, and repairs it when sites change. The product must be secure, observable, testable, accessible, and maintainable by a professional team for years.
meta.quality_bar: Every change must be something a senior engineer would approve in code review. No placeholders, no invented APIs, no fake tests, no decorative comments, no dead code, no speculative abstractions.

context_protocol.purpose: Gemini must carry full project context across sessions, so context is stored in files, not in memory of the chat.

required_files.PROJECT_BRIEF.md: Mission, users, scope, non-goals, success metrics. Owner-edited, agent-read.
required_files.ARCHITECTURE.md: Current system design with Mermaid diagrams; updated in the same commit as any structural change.
required_files.REPO_MAP_<repo>.md: For each vendor repo (chromium, freellmapi, omniroute, rea): purpose, entry points, build/run commands, public interfaces, license, pinned commit, how it is integrated, known risks. Generated by reading real source, with file paths cited.
required_files.DECISIONS/ADR-NNNN-<title>.md: Architecture Decision Records: context, options, decision, consequences. Required for every non-trivial choice.
required_files.GLOSSARY.md: Project terms (skill, run, trace, policy, profile, gateway, provider) with exact definitions.
required_files.BUILD_STATE.json: Machine-readable loop state: phase, tasks, failures, open issues, next_action, last_commit.
required_files.OPEN_QUESTIONS.md: Unknowns and assumptions, each with owner and how it will be resolved.
required_files.CHANGELOG.md: Keep a Changelog format, Semantic Versioning.

session_start_ritual: Read PROJECT_BRIEF.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, GLOSSARY.md, BUILD_STATE.json, OPEN_QUESTIONS.md, and the latest 10 ADRs.
Read the REPO_MAP files for every component the current task touches.
Run git status and git log -20, and run the test suite to establish a baseline.
State the current task, the files expected to change, and the acceptance test, then begin.
session_end_ritual: Update BUILD_STATE.json, ARCHITECTURE.md, CHANGELOG.md, and any ADR affected.
Ensure the working tree is clean and all tests pass or failures are recorded with cause.
Write the exact next_action so a fresh session can continue with zero re-discovery.
context_hygiene: Never rely on remembered facts about a repo; re-read the source and cite file paths.
When a file in /CONTEXT conflicts with the code, the code is the truth: fix the document in the same change.
Keep each context file under 800 lines; split by topic and link between them.

source_repositories.rule: Clone each repo into /vendor/<name> at a pinned tag or commit. Read README, LICENSE, build docs, and entry points before integrating. Record findings in /CONTEXT/REPO_MAP_<name>.md. Respect all licenses; maintain THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES and an SBOM.

repos.role: Browser engine and shell. Phase A: Chromium-based app with a Manifest V3 side-panel extension and Chrome DevTools Protocol control. Phase B (only if hardware allows): maintained patch-set on a pinned stable release, rebased on every Chromium stable security release.
repos.constraints: Full builds need 100GB+ disk, large RAM, and hours of compile time. Never diverge from upstream without a patch queue.

repos.role: One provider adapter behind the model gateway.
repos.constraints: Use only within upstream providers' terms. No key or account pooling to evade limits.

repos.role: Model gateway: routing, fallback, retry, load balancing, rate-limit handling behind one OpenAI-compatible local endpoint.
repos.constraints: Treat as an external service boundary with a versioned client interface.

repos.role: Authorized site and network analysis to improve skill generation and repair.
repos.constraints: No bypassing authentication, paywalls, anti-bot systems, or site terms.

core: Browser with persistent side panel, command bar, and voice input.
Agent mode: plan, act, verify across tabs, forms, downloads, uploads, and extraction.
Observe-and-learn mode: record a demonstration with secrets masked and convert it to a skill.
Auto skill creation, matching, reuse, versioning, self-repair, and natural-language editing.
Scheduler and triggers with background and headless execution.
Local encrypted memory and credential vault, fully user-controlled.
Task replay with screenshots, dry-run, pause, resume, kill switch, undo where possible.
Per-site permission profiles and action risk classification.
Skill import and export with signature verification and a review step before first run.
Cost, token, and latency dashboard per task and provider.
long_term_user_needs: Profile and skill export/import for device migration and backup.
Skill schema migrations so skills created today still run in future versions.
Stable public skill format and plugin API with semantic versioning and a documented deprecation policy (minimum two minor releases of warning).
LTS release channel alongside stable and beta; staged rollouts with automatic rollback on error-rate regression.
Offline queueing, retry with exponential backoff and jitter, and idempotent runs.
Clear user-facing explanations of every action taken and why.

layers: Browser Shell (Chromium) and Side Panel UI
Control Layer (CDP client: accessibility tree first, DOM second, screenshot/vision fallback)
Agent Core (planner, executor, verifier, critic) with deterministic replay
Skill Engine (library, matcher, runner, recorder, generator, repairer, migrator)
Model Gateway (OmniRoute client, provider adapters including FreeLLMAPI, local model option)
Memory and Vault (encrypted at rest, per-profile keys)
Policy and Safety Engine (permissions, confirmations, injection defense, audit log)
Observability (OpenTelemetry traces, metrics, structured logs; local-first, opt-in export)
principles: Process isolation: agent core, gateway client, and skill runner run out of the renderer process, with least privilege.
All page content is untrusted data, never instructions.
Every agent action is idempotent or guarded, logged, and attributable to a plan step.
Typed interfaces at every boundary; schema validation on all model output and all skill files.
Circuit breakers, timeouts, and bulkheads around every external call.
Configuration via versioned config files and feature flags; no hidden behavior.

security: Threat model (STRIDE) written in /CONTEXT/THREAT_MODEL.md and reviewed each phase.
OWASP ASVS L2 as baseline; OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications addressed explicitly (prompt injection, insecure output handling, excessive agency, sensitive information disclosure).
Secrets scanning, SAST, dependency vulnerability scanning, and SBOM generation in CI; builds fail on high or critical findings.
Strict Content Security Policy for extension pages; minimal Manifest V3 permissions with written justification for each.
Plugin and imported-skill sandboxing; signed releases and signed skills; verified updates.
Fuzz testing of parsers (skill loader, recorder, schema validators).
SECURITY.md with coordinated disclosure process; security patch SLA documented.
privacy: Local-first by default; telemetry opt-in and documented field by field.
Data minimization, configurable retention, one-click export and deletion.
GDPR and CCPA aligned data handling; no secrets or personal data in prompts, logs, or crash reports.
Clear disclosure of which provider receives which data.
reliability: Define SLOs: task success rate, p95 action latency, crash-free sessions (target 99.5%+), skill repair success rate.
Crash reporting and automatic checkpoint recovery for running tasks.
Chaos and failure-injection tests: provider outage, network loss, DOM change, tab crash, disk full.
Backup and restore for the profile store with tested migration paths.
testing: Test pyramid: unit, integration, end-to-end on local deterministic test sites, plus a live-site smoke suite behind a flag.
LLM evaluation harness: a golden task set with pass/fail scoring, tracked per release; regressions block release.
Deterministic replay of recorded runs for debugging.
Coverage reported; flaky tests quarantined with a ticket and a deadline, never ignored.
Security regression suite of at least 50 injection and abuse cases.
performance: Budgets enforced in CI: cold start, memory per tab, agent step latency, tokens per task.
accessibility_and_i18n: WCAG 2.2 AA for all browser-owned UI; full keyboard operation and screen-reader support.
Internationalization from day one with externalized strings; English and Bangla shipped first; RTL-ready.
release_engineering: Trunk-based development with short-lived branches, Conventional Commits, protected main, required reviews and checks.
Reproducible builds, code signing, and macOS notarization and Windows signing where applicable.
Update framework with staged rollout, kill-switch, and rollback.
Release channels: nightly, beta, stable, LTS.
Chromium security rebase cadence documented and automated.
documentation_and_operations: README, USER_GUIDE, DEVELOPER_GUIDE, SKILL_AUTHORING_GUIDE, SECURITY, PRIVACY, CONTRIBUTING, CODE_OF_CONDUCT, SUPPORT.
Runbooks for incident response, release, rollback, and key rotation.
Public API and skill-format reference generated from schemas.
legal_and_compliance: License audit for every dependency and vendor repo; incompatibilities block the build.
THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES generated and verified in CI.
Terms-of-service-aware automation: official APIs preferred; no circumvention of access controls.

anti_slop_rules: Do not write code you have not run. Do not claim a test passed unless you saw it pass.
Do not invent function names, flags, endpoints, or config keys. Verify them in the actual source or official documentation and cite the file path.
Do not add comments that restate the code. Comment only the why, constraints, and non-obvious tradeoffs.
Do not create placeholder files, empty stubs, TODOs in shipped paths, or mock implementations presented as real.
Do not write tests that assert nothing, mirror the implementation, or hard-code expected outputs to pass.
Do not add dependencies without an ADR entry covering license, maintenance health, size, and alternatives.
Do not generalize prematurely; build the simplest design that meets the acceptance criteria and the documented extension points.
Do not use marketing language, emojis, or filler in code, docs, commits, or reports.
Prefer small, reviewable commits; each commit builds, passes tests, and has one purpose.
When uncertain, say so in OPEN_QUESTIONS.md, choose the safest reversible option, and continue.

loop: SELECT the highest-priority unfinished task in the current phase.
DESIGN: write or update the ADR and acceptance test first for any non-trivial task.
IMPLEMENT in small commits following engineering conventions.
VERIFY: build, lint, type-check, unit, integration, e2e, security scans, performance budgets.
ON FAILURE: find root cause, fix, re-run. After 5 distinct failed approaches, log in OPEN_QUESTIONS.md with evidence and move to non-dependent work.
REVIEW: act as a skeptical reviewer on your own diff covering correctness, security, performance, accessibility, licensing, and maintainability.
DOCUMENT: update /CONTEXT files, CHANGELOG, and user or developer docs in the same change.
REPEAT until the phase gate passes; then run the phase gate review and advance.
master_loop.decision_policy: Make reasonable implementation decisions autonomously and record them as ADRs. Do not wait for approval on engineering choices. Stop only on stop_conditions.

phases.name: Discovery, Context, and Foundations
tasks: Clone and pin all vendor repos; produce REPO_MAP files from real source.
Write PROJECT_BRIEF, ARCHITECTURE, GLOSSARY, THREAT_MODEL, initial ADRs.
Detect hardware and choose Chromium strategy.
Set up monorepo, CI, linters, formatters, pre-commit hooks, secrets scanning, SBOM, license checks, and a one-command dev setup.
gate: All context files exist and match the code
CI green on an empty-feature baseline

phases.name: Browser Shell and Control Layer
tasks: Branded Chromium-based shell with side panel and command bar.
CDP control layer with accessibility-tree-first observation and robust multi-strategy targeting.
Deterministic local test sites for e2e.

phases.name: Model Gateway
tasks: OmniRoute integration behind a versioned client interface.
FreeLLMAPI adapter and provider interface for others including local models.
Structured-output validation, timeouts, circuit breakers, failover, cost and latency logging.
gate: Forced provider failure triggers automatic failover
Schema-invalid model output is rejected and retried safely

phases.name: Agent Core
tasks: Planner, executor, verifier, critic loop with checkpointing and deterministic replay.
Pause, resume, kill switch, crash recovery.
LLM evaluation harness with a golden task set.
gate: At least 85% success on the golden suite of 30+ tasks

phases.name: Skill Engine and Learning
tasks: Skill library, matcher, runner, versioning, schema migrations.
Recorder with secret masking; generator from runs and demonstrations; repairer for broken steps.
REA-assisted authorized site analysis; signed import and export.
gate: Second run of a learned task uses the skill with no replanning of stable steps
Injected selector break is repaired, tested, and saved as a new version

phases.name: Safety, Privacy, and Policy
tasks: Permission profiles, risk classification, confirmation policies.
Prompt-injection defenses and untrusted-content handling.
Encrypted vault and memory; audit log; export and deletion.
Captcha and 2FA hand-off to the user then automatic resume.
gate: No secrets found in logs, traces, or crash reports by automated scan

phases.name: Automation, Scheduling, and UX
tasks: Scheduler, triggers, background and headless runs, parallel queue with resource limits.
Replay viewer, dry-run, undo, data export, voice input, i18n (English, Bangla).
Accessibility pass to WCAG 2.2 AA.
gate: Scheduled skill runs unattended for a simulated 24 hours with retries and a report

phases.name: Hardening and Release Engineering
tasks: Chaos and fuzz testing; performance profiling against budgets.
Signed installers for Windows, macOS, Linux; update framework with staged rollout and rollback.
Runbooks, full documentation set, SECURITY.md, deprecation policy, LTS channel definition.
gate: Clean install on fresh VMs works end to end
All SLO dashboards and budgets pass

phases.name: Sustainment (continuous)
tasks: Monthly Chromium rebase and dependency updates with full regression run.
Skill-format backward-compatibility tests against all prior schema versions.
Triage user-reported failures into new golden tasks.
gate: Every release passes the regression, security, and migration suites

stop_conditions: A required action would violate law, a site's access controls, or the safety boundaries.
A license forbids the intended use.
A destructive action outside the project directory would be required.
A decision is irreversible and has materially different outcomes for the owner (for example paid services, publishing releases, or accepting legal terms): prepare the options in an ADR and stop.
safety_boundaries: The agent hands captchas, 2FA, and security prompts to the user for that single step and then resumes; it never defeats them.
Payments, deletions, outbound messages, account changes, and publishing require pre-authorized policy or explicit confirmation.
Operate only with the user's own authorized accounts.
Use free LLM providers only within their terms.

reporting.per_phase: PHASE_REPORT_<n>.md: scope delivered, test and scan results, metrics against budgets, ADRs added, known issues, next phase plan.
reporting.final: FINAL_REPORT.md: architecture, requirement traceability matrix, benchmark and eval results, security assessment, operational runbook index, and a prioritized roadmap.

start_command: Create /CONTEXT, generate the required context files from the real source of the four repos, set BUILD_STATE.json to phase 0, and run the master_loop continuously until all phase gates pass or a stop_condition is reached.
